review_candidates.description: Titre de la position MMC Project Officer Supervisée par MMC Data and Research Project Manager West and North Africa Répondant à MMC Data and Research Project Manager West and North Africa Duty Station Dakar Area of Operation West and North Africa Période considérée 1 January 2027 – 31 December 2027 Type de contrat National Salary & Benefits NMH Background The MMC is a global research centre consisting of five regional hubs (Asia, East Africa and Southern Africa, Europe, West and North Africa, Latin America and Caribbean) and a central unit in Geneva and Copenhagen. The MMC is a leading source for independent and high-quality data, research, analysis and expertise on mixed migration. The MMC aims to increase understanding of mixed migration, to positively impact global and regional migration policies, to inform evidence-based programming responses for people on the move and to stimulate forward thinking in public and policy debates on mixed migration. The MMC’s overarching focus is on human rights and protection for all people on the move. The three overall objectives of the MMC are: To contribute to a better, more nuanced, and balanced understanding of mixed migration (knowledge) To contribute to evidence-based and better-informed migration policies and debates (policy) To contribute to effective evidence-based responses for people on the move (programming) The MMC is part of and governed by DRC. MMC regional hubs are hosted within DRC offices and are part of the global MMC network. While its institutional link to DRC ensures MMC’s work is grounded in operational reality, it acts as an independent source of data, research, analysis and policy development on mixed migration for policy makers, practitioners, journalists, and the broader humanitarian sector. The position of the MMC does not necessarily reflect the position of DRC. For more information on MMC visit our website (http://www.mixedmigration.org). Mixed Migration Mixed migration refers to cross-border movements of people including refugees fleeing persecution and conflict, victims of trafficking and people seeking better lives and opportunities. Motivated to move by a multiplicity of factors, people engaged in such movements have different legal statuses as well as a variety of vulnerabilities. Although entitled to protection under international human rights law, they are exposed to multiple rights violations along their journey. Those in mixed migration flows travel along similar routes, using similar means of travel - often travelling irregularly and wholly or partially assisted by migrant smugglers. The West and North Africa Region MMC West and North Africa (WANA) form one region under the direct supervision of the MMC Regional Manager for the WANA region based in Dakar, Senegal. MMC WANA is currently directly collecting data in several countries in North and West Africa through its flagship 4Mi methodology. The MMC is a research institution engaging with policy makers, (I)NGOs, CSOs at both country-level and through regional mechanisms. Key research themes include onward movement and migration decision-making, children and youth in mobility, smuggling of migrants, urban migration, use of social media, returns and reintegration, and climate change and migration. Other thematics might arise and MMC research remains agile to respond to pressing needs for evidence-based programming and policy development. The MMC WANA regional team is positioned primarily in Dakar, with some team members based in other locations across the region. The MMC regional manager sits in Dakar, along with the Data & Research Project Manager, the Information Management Specialist, the Regional Research Specialist, and the MMC Finance Specialist. Field Research Operations and Coordination Contribute to and draft field and research protocols under the close supervision of the Data & Research Project Manager. Support the Data & Research Project Manager and Coordinators in meeting operational needs and addressing operational challenges in countries, including but not limited to authorizations for activities, reporting on activities to institutions as per mandatory processes, and adjusting operational modalities. Support the scoping and establishment of new and recurring partnerships for field implementation, including through vetting, due diligence, and contracting processes. review_candidates.description: Job Description Title: Outreach/Triage Nurse Classification: Full-Time/Exempt Schedule: Monday-Friday, 8:00am-5:00pm Locations: This position will work between the following locations: Hope Haven: Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays (24 hours/week) Ophelia Garmon-Brown Medical Clinic: Tuesdays and Fridays (16 hours/week) Position Summary The Outreach/Triage Nurse will provide patient education, assess patient status/prioritize care accordingly, and provide outreach to patients who face barriers to care, have chronic health conditions, and have complex medical needs. This position encompasses direct patient care and patient education/advocacy. The individual in this role will work between two locations: Hope Haven (outreach) and Charlotte Community Health Clinic’s Ophelia-Garmon Brown Medical Clinic (triage). CCHC Core Requirements Patient Centered Customer Service – Whether directly or indirectly, we work to support the delivery of an excellent patient experience to everyone served by the organization. Caring and Compassion – We provide empathic comfort to those in distress and share kindness in all interpersonal interactions. Respectful Communication – We communicate openly, honestly and without judgment while honoring each individual’s uniqueness and assuming the best of those with whom we interact. Teamwork – We are members of a diverse interdisciplinary team working together to meet a common goal. Accountability – We accept our individual and team responsibilities, and we meet our commitments. We take responsibility for our performance and actions. Customer Safety – We recognize and correct potential hazards to protect our customers and ourselves. Key Responsibilities Patient Outreach: Provides patient education, outreach, and clinical support to improve access to care and promote positive patient outcomes. This position serves patients experiencing homelessness/instability, those with chronic diseases, patients experiencing substance use challenges, individuals who are in a transitional period in their life/medical journey, those with food insecurity, etc. Provides age-specific patient care by assessing, implementing, evaluating, and documenting patient needs, nursing actions taken, and patient responses to care. Updates patient chart. Gathers information, reviews past allergic reactions, administers medications and treatments within scope of practice. Shares patient information with provider to facilitate care evaluations and follows direction from provider. Makes patient referrals as directed by the provider, to resolve identified problems or reach established patient goals. Reviews orders for clarity and appropriateness. Reaches out to patients who are overdue for or have missed appointments to re-engage. Identifies patients who will benefit from community resources and care management. Identifies patient learning needs, incorporates into care by providing education and counsel to patients, and documents patient understanding; Helps to facilitate that care provided is consistent with policies, procedures and telephone triage protocols, in cooperation with the physician; Able to function in emergency situations and facilitates the care provided for all patients; Provides high-quality, safe, and thorough patient care. Serves as an advocate for the patient. Maintains all appropriate licensure. Understands and follows HIPAA guidelines and regulations. Ensures all test results, in-house and referred, are reported to the provider by checking a manifest or providing oversight of pending labs. Performs CLIA waived tests. Participates in community events, health fairs, medical screenings, etc. as needed. Performs other duties as assigned. Triage Evaluates incoming patients in person and over the phone to determine the urgency of their needs and prioritize care based on their condition(s). Provides treatments, administers vaccines, etc. as needed and within scope. Provides age-specific patient care by assessing, implementing, evaluating, and documenting the individual patient's needs, actions taken and the patient's responses relative to nursing care; Shares patient information with the provider to facilitate care evaluations and updates data in the medical record; Accepts direction from the provider; Makes patient referrals as directed by the provider, and as appropriate, to resolve identified problems or reach established patient goals; Reviews orders for clarity and appropriateness. Gathers information, reviews past allergic reactions. Administers medications and treatments within the scope of practice, uses approved policies/procedures/protocols. Displays critical thinking skills to determine appropriate care. Considers patient/family beliefs/differences and incorporates them into patient care. Identifies patient learning needs, incorporates them into care by providing education and counsel to patients, and documents patient understanding. Knowledgeable of growth and development of an individual’s life stages. Able to function in emergency situations and facilitate the care provided for all patients. Serves as an advocate for the patient. Understands and follows HIPAA guidelines and ensures the confidentiality of patient results; Ensures all test results, in-house and referred, are reported to the provider by checking a manifest or providing oversight of pending labs. Able to perform CLIA waived tests as needed. Performs other duties as assigned. Minimum Qualifications Associates’ degree in nursing. A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in nursing is preferred. Active and unencumbered NC RN license or multi-state license that encompasses lawful practice in North Carolina. 4+ years of experience in direct patient care/triage, preferably primary care. Current BLS certification. Must be obtained within 90 days of employment. Prior experience with Epic is a plus. Other Skills, Knowledge, And Abilities Excellent communication skills, both written and oral. Ability to work independently and collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team. Proficient with electronic health records (Epic highly preferred). Maintain the highest level of confidentiality and follow all HIPAA regulations. Bilingual in Spanish and English highly preferred. Experience working in an FQHC environment is highly preferred. Ability to pivot and adapt in a fast-paced healthcare environment. Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite. Accepts and learns from constructive criticism. Maintain continuous education to stay current with healthcare best practices and new technology. Ability to effectively work with patients, colleagues, community partners, etc. that come from various backgrounds. Must have reliable transportation and valid NC driver’s license. Ability to travel between multiple sites as needed. All duties and responsibilities are subject to possible modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities. The physical demands associated with this position include but are not limited to: frequent lifting, bending, climbing, stooping, and pulling; frequent repetitive motions; continuous standing and walking; repetitive movement of hands and fingers (typing and/or writing); lifting of greater than 50 pounds. The noise level in the work environment is low, consistent with that of a typical office. Charlotte Community Health Clinic, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate in any aspect of employment with regard to age, race, sex, national origin, disability, color, marital status, veteran’s status, or religion.
